_comment: Pinned sources for the Warp on-device toolchain (arm64 Android).
Nothing here is committed as a binary — build_toolchain.py fetches each
item, checks its SHA-256 against this file, and assembles the bundle.
A null sha256 means 'not pinned yet': the script prints the real hash so
it can be pasted in. Never leave a null in a release build.

sdk_tools._why: aapt2 + zipalign. Statically linked AArch64 ELF executables, so they
sdk_tools._why2: run from any directory with no shared-library or prefix dependencies.

jdk._why: kotlinc and d8 are Java programs, so the phone needs a real JVM.
jdk._why2: Termux builds are compiled for /data/data/com.termux/... but 58 of 62
jdk._why3: ELF files already carry $ORIGIN in RUNPATH, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH is
jdk._why4: searched before RUNPATH, so the runtime relocates into Warp's dir.

support_libs._why: Shared libraries the JVM needs that are NOT inside the JDK package.
support_libs._why2: libandroid-shmem is required by libjvm.so, libandroid-spawn by libjava.so.
support_libs._why3: Android has libz.so but the JDK asks for libz.so.1, hence zlib.

items._why: The NDK C++ runtime. Android does NOT provide it — apps ship it.
items._why2: Missing this made the JVM fail on the device with:
items.name: libc++

kotlin._why: Pure JVM bytecode, so it is CPU-architecture independent.
kotlin._why2: Must match the Kotlin version the app itself is built with.

r8._why: d8 turns .class files into .dex. Also pure JVM bytecode.

android_jar._why: The compile-time Android API surface. Taken from the LOCAL SDK, not
android_jar._why2: downloaded, because the Android SDK licence restricts redistribution.
android_jar._why3: Anyone building the bundle must have the platform installed locally.
android_jar.license: Android SDK Terms and Conditions (not redistributable)

jdk_trim._why: Shrinks the bundle. None of these are needed to run kotlinc or d8.
jdk_trim._why2: legal/ is deliberately KEPT so licence texts ship with the binaries.
